review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the repo for uses of heatFlow_nonpositive, heatFlow_joint_continuous and the heatFlow definitions. I also checked heatOperator_zero in SobolevHeat.lean, which is already @[simp]. I found no competing rules, loops or wrongly oriented rewrites. heatFlow_nonpositive has a side condition and is used by explicit rw in two places, so making it simp is not clearly justified. The one real gap is that derivativeIntegrand is an indicator-valued def with no unfolding lemmas, so both branches of shiftedHeat_value_hasDerivAt unfold it by hand with a long simpa only list. The evidence for this is only the two uses in this file. I did not check downstream files that may use derivativeIntegrand, and I have not run Lean.

findings.problem: derivativeIntegrand is defined as an indicator of Iic t, but the file has no unfolding lemmas for it. Each branch of shiftedHeat_value_hasDerivAt therefore unfolds the definition by hand. It does this with a long, fragile `simpa only` list (indicator, mem_Iic, ite_true/ite_false, one_smul/smul_zero, Function.comp_def, id_eq) that depends on the internal indicator form. Any other consumer of derivativeIntegrand, such as fullDuhamel_value_hasDerivAt or later files, would have to repeat this unfolding. Nothing states the intended normal forms: the value is ν • laplacianEvaluation … for s ≤ t, and 0 for t < s.
findings.proposed_change: Add two lemmas stating the case values, for example `derivativeIntegrand_of_le (h : s ≤ t) : derivativeIntegrand period hq ν T hT f t s = ν • laplacianEvaluation period q hq (heatFlow period q ν (t - s) (extendPath T hT f s))` and `derivativeIntegrand_of_gt (h : t < s) : derivativeIntegrand … t s = 0`. Prove them with `Set.indicator_of_mem` (resp. `Set.indicator_of_notMem`). Mark them @[simp] (a conditional rewrite that simp can discharge) or at least use them via `simp [derivativeIntegrand_of_le hst.le]`. The two `simpa only [derivativeIntegrand, indicator, …]` calls then shrink to a rewrite with these lemmas plus Function.comp_def. Keep derivativeIntegrand itself non-simp, so that it does not expand unexpectedly.
findings.benefit: The two cases of the parameter derivative get canonical, reusable rewrite rules. Proofs no longer depend on how indicator unfolds into `ite`, and simp does not have to expose the indicator/ite form.
